text.p: The following are the main stories from Monday morning's Austrian newspapers:

- Michael Haeupl, Vienna's mayor, says Social Democrats should work together with the far-right Freedom Party in Parliament if it should prove useful, but rules out a coalition between the two parties.

- Tyrol's Social Democrat party chief Herbert Prock has confirmed an offer by designated Chancellor Viktor Klima to take over the party management, replacing Brigitte Ederer who will move into the Vienna city government.
- Parting Social Affairs Minister Franz Hums has drafted a law to ensure benefits are continued for employees of bankrupt firms.
- Social Democrats are against plans to move the Science agenda to a new conservative-controlled Educational Ministry.
- Skimaker Kaestle's production plant in Hohenems might be closed down as machinery has been moved by its owner, Italy's Benetton.
- Austria's current account can only be saved by higher exports as tourism is losing ground, according to research institute IHS head Bernhard Felderer.
- If Herbert Prock does not accept the position of chief manager of the Social Democrat party, Styrian Guenther Doerflinger could be offered the job.
- Experts expect speedier reforms and competition with junior coalition partner conservative People's Party over Austria's European policies after Viktor Klima becomes Chancellor.
- Miner VA-Bergtechnik might cut 600 jobs at its Austrian plant as its parent Finland's Tampella is deeply in the red.
- All bids for the state-owned salt monopoly Salinen AG must be handed in by February 7.
- The price of 400 schillings per share for GiroCredit being asked by its major shareholder AVZ is not feasible as it is only worth 200 schillings based on its 1995 balance sheet, the newspaper says.
- Klima is highly praised abroad and compared to U.S. president Bill Clinton.
